What Makes Morning People Happier Than Others?

answer_raw:
Morning-type people tend to report higher levels of happiness and life satisfaction than night owls [1][2][7].

Research suggests that "morningness" is associated with greater happiness emotions across different age groups [1]. Morning types often report feeling more **healthy**, **cheerful**, **lively**, and **alert** [1][2]. This correlation may exist because morning people are naturally aligned with their internal clocks, leading to better sleep quality [1].

The link between timing and happiness is not an absolute rule; morning types do not necessarily report lower levels of nervousness or distress than night owls [2]. Additionally, the tendency toward being a night owl often fades as people age, which may explain why older adults often report higher happiness levels than younger adults [7].

I didn't find whether a night owl can biologically switch their chronotype, so you would need to look into circadian rhythm entrainment or chronotherapy.
